headline: Softer volumes weigh on results despite margin recovery
summary_short: PulteGroup reported Q2 FY2026 total revenue of $3,983M, up 16.9% q/q but down 9.6% y/y, with diluted EPS of $2.48 (+38.5% q/q, -18.2% y/y) as home sale gross margin expanded 60bp sequentially to 25.0% despite an 8% y/y drop in closings.
summary_long: Home sale revenue fell 11% y/y to $3.8B as closings dropped 8% to 6,997 homes and average price fell 3% to $544,000; total revenue still rose 16.9% q/q on the seasonal step-up from Q1. Home sale gross margin was 25.0%, down from 27.0% y/y but up 60bp sequentially, as SG&A rose to 10.1% of home sale revenue (9.1% prior year). Net income of $472M and diluted EPS of $2.48 fell 22% and 18% y/y, but rose 36% and 39% q/q as Q1's slower season passed. Net new orders rose 6% y/y to 7,536 homes on 8% more communities. Cash fell to $1.3B (-26% q/q) after $373M of buybacks; equity was $13.0B (+3.5% y/y).

drivers.explanation: Home sale revenue fell 11% y/y on an 8% decline in closings to 6,997 homes and a 3% decrease in average selling price to $544,000; total revenue still rose q/q as Q2 outpaced Q1's slower season.
Home sale gross margin of 25.0% is down from 27.0% a year ago but up 60 basis points sequentially from Q1, as the company balanced price and pace within each community.
Lower home sale revenue and gross margin versus a stronger prior-year quarter drove the y/y decline; a smaller diluted share count from $373M of buybacks partly offset the drop in EPS.

Management cites a highly competitive backdrop of macro uncertainty, volatile rates, and strained affordability, with only early signs of stabilization in select geographies; the company is making tactical price/pace adjustments by community.
